title: The Opposing Good
logline: A person who once did real harm now spends every day doing quiet, repeated service at a community kitchen, without ever explaining why to the people they serve.
human_question: Can steady, ordinary good work actually answer for something done long before?

premise.story: A volunteer's daily routine at a community kitchen or shelter, and, in their own words and own time, why they do this particular work now.
premise.place: A community kitchen or shelter in a northern town.
premise.experience: Unglamorous daily tasks, chopping, serving, cleaning up, repeated with real steadiness, and a person's own account, offered only if and when they choose, of what led them here.

concept_links.why: The source advises that someone who has done wrong should deliberately take up the opposing good, because a later strong action can weaken an earlier one's force [C055-M:L32-L34]. The film follows someone living that out in their own terms, without ever narrating their past for them.
Whatever the past harm was, the ten courses of harm this source sets out [C058-M:L3] give the film's viewer, without a single word of doctrine, the sense that harm has a shape and a weight.

what_camera_could_observe: The person's manner with those they serve
A quiet conversation about the present rather than the past
The routine repeated across different days
what_must_be_real: A real volunteer with real, ongoing consent to reveal as much or as little of their own history as they choose. The film never demands or reconstructs their past.

possible_arc.opening: An ordinary morning at the kitchen.
possible_arc.turn: A moment where the person is asked, gently, why they do this.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever they choose to answer, or not. The routine continues either way.

requirements: A community kitchen or shelter with a long-term volunteer willing to be filmed and to control their own story
Full consent over what personal history, if any, is disclosed

suggestions.name: A community kitchen or shelter in Jaffna or Vavuniya
suggestions.why: Suggested for northern geographic representation; no specific organisation identified.

risks: Exposing a real person's past without their full, ongoing consent
Turning the film into a redemption narrative that the person has not chosen for themselves
Any past victims' privacy and feelings
drop_if: No volunteer will participate under these consent conditions
The story would require disclosing details the person does not want shared

connections.note: A different response to the same pressure explored in The Boundary Walk: repair through service rather than dispute over property.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
